children.title: Log-Sum-Exp Graphs
children.top_down_role: Graph constructions for logarithms of finite exponential sums.

assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge \operatorname{lse}(x)\iff \exists u\in\mathbb{R}_+^n:\ \sum_{i=1}^n u_i\le 1,\ (x_i-t,1,u_i)\in K_{\exp}\ \forall i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential-cone representation of the closed epigraph of finite-dimensional log-sum-exp.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), define \(\operatorname{lse}(x)=\log(\sum_{i=1}^n e^{x_i})\). Its epigraph has the exponential-cone representation
\[
 t\ge \operatorname{lse}(x)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists u\in\mathbb{R}_+^n:\ \sum_{i=1}^n u_i\le 1,
 \qquad (x_i-t,1,u_i)\in K_{\exp}\quad(i=1,\ldots,n),
\]
where \(K_{\exp}=\operatorname{cl}\{(a,b,c):b>0,\ b\exp(a/b)\le c\}\). Thus the log-sum-exp epigraph is the projection of an affine slice of a product of exponential cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The epigraph of log-sum-exp is represented by one exponential-cone constraint per coordinate and a single sum constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Log-Sum-Exp Graphs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exponential-cone epigraph formula is mathematically coherent and fits the representation container, but no citation or inspectable locator supports it.

children.title: Soft-Max Graphs
children.top_down_role: Graph constructions associated with smooth maximum surrogates and normalized exponential weighting.

assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=\nabla f_\tau(x)\iff p_i=e^{x_i/\tau}/\sum_j e^{x_j/\tau}\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph of the temperature-scaled soft-max mapping, viewed as the gradient of log-sum-exp.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\tau>0\), define \(f_\tau(x)=\tau\log(\sum_{j=1}^n\exp(x_j/\tau))\). The soft-max graph is
\[
\operatorname{gra}(\nabla f_\tau)
 =\left\{(x,p)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\Delta_n:
 p_i=\frac{\exp(x_i/\tau)}{\sum_{j=1}^n\exp(x_j/\tau)}
 \text{ for }i=1,\ldots,n\right\}.
\]
Every graph point satisfies \(p_i>0\), and conversely \((x,p)\) lies in the graph exactly when there exists \(c\in\mathbb{R}\) such that \(x_i=\tau\log p_i+c\) for all \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Soft-max maps a score vector to positive simplex weights and is the gradient of temperature-scaled log-sum-exp.
knowledge_statements.title: Soft-Max Graphs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The soft-max graph and inverse-up-to-shift characterization are coherent, though the definition content kind is debatable for a graph representation. No supporting citation or locator is supplied.

children.title: Shift-Invariant Representations
children.top_down_role: Equivalent graph forms organized around common affine shifts of exponential arguments.

assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\)
\(c\in\mathbb{R}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_\tau(x+c\mathbf{1})=f_\tau(x)+c\) and \(\nabla f_\tau(x+c\mathbf{1})=\nabla f_\tau(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Translation equivariance of log-sum-exp and translation invariance of its soft-max gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_\tau(x)=\tau\log(\sum_{i=1}^n\exp(x_i/\tau))\) with \(\tau>0\). For every \(c\in\mathbb{R}\),
\[
f_\tau(x+c\mathbf{1})=f_\tau(x)+c,
\qquad
\nabla f_\tau(x+c\mathbf{1})=\nabla f_\tau(x).
\]
Consequently, with \(m=\max_i x_i\), the equivalent representation
\[
f_\tau(x)=m+\tau\log\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^n\exp((x_i-m)/\tau)\right)
\]
has nonpositive exponential arguments and preserves the associated soft-max vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common score shift translates log-sum-exp by that shift but leaves soft-max unchanged, enabling stable max-shifted evaluation.
knowledge_statements.title: Shift-Invariant Representations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The shift identities and max-shifted representation are correct in form and fit this property container, but they have no cited source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Extreme-Scale Regimes
children.top_down_role: Graph behavior when exponential arguments have widely separated scales.

assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_i x_i\le f_\tau(x)\le\max_i x_i+\tau\log n\) and \(\lim_{\tau\downarrow0}f_\tau(x)=\max_i x_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero- and infinite-temperature limits for scaled log-sum-exp and soft-max.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f_\tau(x)=\tau\log(\sum_{i=1}^n\exp(x_i/\tau))\),
\[
\max_i x_i\le f_\tau(x)\le\max_i x_i+\tau\log n,
\qquad
\lim_{\tau\downarrow0}f_\tau(x)=\max_i x_i.
\]
If \(p_\tau=\nabla f_\tau(x)\), then \(p_\tau\) converges as \(\tau\downarrow0\) to the uniform distribution on \(I(x)=\{i:x_i=\max_jx_j\}\). As \(\tau\to\infty\), \(p_\tau\to\mathbf{1}/n\), while \(f_\tau(x)-\tau\log n\to n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Low temperature yields the maximum and concentrates soft-max on maximizers; high temperature yields uniform weights and the centered arithmetic mean.
knowledge_statements.title: Extreme-Scale Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-temperature bounds and stated low- and high-temperature limits are coherent, but no source or locator supports the complete collection of claims.

children.title: Negative-Entropy Graphs
children.top_down_role: Graph forms for scalar and separable negative entropy.

assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\)
\(t\in\mathbb{R}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge\sum_i x_i\log x_i\iff\exists t_i:\sum_i t_i\le t,\ (-t_i,x_i,1)\in K_{\exp}\ \forall i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar and separable closed negative entropy on the nonnegative orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(h:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}\) by \(h(x)=x\log x\) for \(x>0\) and \(h(0)=0\). Its epigraph satisfies
\[
t\ge h(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(-t,x,1)\in K_{\exp}.
\]
For the separable function \(H(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n h(x_i)\) on \(\mathbb{R}_+^n\),
\[
t\ge H(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists t_1,\ldots,t_n:\ \sum_{i=1}^n t_i\le t,
\quad(-t_i,x_i,1)\in K_{\exp}\quad(i=1,\ldots,n).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scalar and separable negative-entropy epigraphs are represented by exponential cones, using the closed convention that zero log zero equals zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Entropy Graphs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar and separable negative-entropy exponential-cone representations are coherent and match the graph-form container, but no supporting citation is provided.

children.title: Relative-Entropy Graphs
children.top_down_role: Joint graph forms for scalar or vector relative-entropy expressions.

assumptions_latex: \(t\in\mathbb{R}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge\operatorname{relentr}(x,y)\iff(-t,x,y)\in K_{\exp}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed scalar relative entropy and its exact exponential-cone epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The closed scalar relative-entropy function is
\[
\operatorname{relentr}(x,y)=
\begin{cases}
x\log(x/y),&x>0,\ y>0,\\
0,&x=0,\ y\ge0,\\
+\infty,&x>0,\ y=0,
\end{cases}
\]
with value \(+\infty\) outside \(\mathbb{R}_+^2\). For finite \(t\), its epigraph is represented exactly by
\[
t\ge\operatorname{relentr}(x,y)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(-t,x,y)\in K_{\exp},
\]
where \(K_{\exp}=\operatorname{cl}\{(a,b,c):b>0,\ b\exp(a/b)\le c\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closed scalar relative entropy has an exact exponential-cone epigraph, including its boundary behavior at zero coordinates.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Entropy Graphs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The closed boundary convention and exponential-cone epigraph orientation are coherent, but the record lacks any source and specific locator.

children.title: Divergence Graphs
children.top_down_role: Graph forms for supported divergence measures derived from entropy structure.

assumptions_latex: \(x,y\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\)
\(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}x=\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}y\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge D(x\|y)\iff\exists t_i:\sum_i t_i\le t,\ (-t_i,x_i,y_i)\in K_{\exp}\ \forall i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential-cone graph of separable relative-entropy divergence for equal-mass nonnegative vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x,y\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\) with equal mass, define \(D(x\|y)=\sum_{i=1}^n\operatorname{relentr}(x_i,y_i)\) using the closed scalar convention. Then
\[
t\ge D(x\|y)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists t\in\mathbb{R}^n:\ \sum_{i=1}^n t_i\le t,
\qquad(-t_i,x_i,y_i)\in K_{\exp}\quad(i=1,\ldots,n).
\]
Moreover, \(D(x\|y)\ge0\), and equality holds exactly when \(x=y\). Without the equal-mass assumption, this nonnegativity assertion need not hold for the unnormalized sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal-mass relative-entropy divergence is nonnegative and its epigraph is the projection of coordinatewise exponential-cone constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Divergence Graphs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The intended separable graph and equal-mass nonnegativity claim are plausible, but the scalar epigraph variable t is absent from the assumptions and is shadowed by the existential vector named t. No source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Zero-Coordinate Regimes
children.top_down_role: Closure conventions and domain behavior when entropy arguments reach zero.

assumptions_latex: \(x,y\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D(x\|y)<+\infty\iff \{i:x_i>0\}\subseteq\{i:y_i>0\}\).

notation.meaning: Positive support of a nonnegative vector.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary conventions and finiteness criterion for coordinatewise relative entropy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For nonnegative vectors \(x,y\), adopt
\[
\operatorname{relentr}(0,y_i)=0\quad(y_i\ge0),
\qquad
\operatorname{relentr}(x_i,0)=+\infty\quad(x_i>0).
\]
Consequently,
\[
D(x\|y)=\sum_{i=1}^n\operatorname{relentr}(x_i,y_i)<+\infty
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{supp}_+(x)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}_+(y).
\]
At a coordinate with \(x_i=y_i=0\), the closed value is zero. Thus a zero reference coordinate excludes positive mass in the first argument, whereas a zero first coordinate contributes zero regardless of the reference coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative entropy is finite exactly when every positive coordinate of its first argument corresponds to a positive coordinate of its second.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Coordinate Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The support-inclusion finiteness criterion and zero-coordinate conventions are coherent and fit the condition container, but no supporting citation or locator is supplied.

children.title: Divergence Asymmetry
children.top_down_role: Structural consequences of argument order in nonsymmetric divergence graphs.

assumptions_latex: \(p,q\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\)
\(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}p=\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}q=1\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D(p\|q)\) need not equal \(D(q\|p)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete demonstration that relative-entropy divergence is not symmetric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p=(1/2,1/2)\) and \(q=(3/4,1/4)\). Both vectors lie in the strictly positive probability simplex, but
\[
D(p\|q)=\frac12\log\frac43,
\qquad
D(q\|p)=\frac34\log\frac32+\frac14\log\frac12.
\]
These quantities are unequal. Hence relative-entropy divergence is generally asymmetric, so exchanging its arguments changes both its value and its epigraph constraint. In particular, \(D(\cdot\|q)\) and \(D(q\|\cdot)\) must not be interchanged during graph canonicalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two strictly positive binary distributions give different forward and reverse relative entropies, proving that the divergence is asymmetric.
knowledge_statements.title: Divergence Asymmetry

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed binary example correctly demonstrates asymmetry and the counterexample kind fits the terminal container, but it has no cited source or inspectable locator.

\(s,t\in\mathbb{R}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge\lambda_{\max}(X)\iff tI-X\succeq0\), and \(s\le\lambda_{\min}(X)\iff X-sI\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semidefinite graph forms for the largest and smallest eigenvalues of a real symmetric matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(X\in\mathbb{S}^n\), the largest-eigenvalue epigraph and smallest-eigenvalue hypograph satisfy
\[
t\ge\lambda_{\max}(X)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
tI-X\succeq0,
\qquad
s\le\lambda_{\min}(X)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
X-sI\succeq0.
\]
Thus both extreme-eigenvalue graph constraints are affine linear matrix inequalities. Equivalently, \(\lambda_{\max}(X)=\min\{t:tI-X\succeq0\}\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(X)=\max\{s:X-sI\succeq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Largest-eigenvalue epigraphs and smallest-eigenvalue hypographs are represented exactly by affine positive-semidefinite inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Extreme-Eigenvalue Graphs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The largest-eigenvalue epigraph and smallest-eigenvalue hypograph LMIs are coherent and fit the representation container, but no supporting citation is supplied.

children.title: Spectral Norm Graphs
children.top_down_role: Graph representations for the largest singular value.

assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\)
\(t\in\mathbb{R}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|X\|_2\le t\iff\begin{pmatrix}tI_m&X\\X^{\mathsf T}&tI_n\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Largest singular value of a matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-semidefinite representation of the spectral-norm epigraph for rectangular real matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), its spectral norm is \(\|X\|_2=\sigma_{\max}(X)\). The epigraph has the exact semidefinite representation
\[
\|X\|_2\le t
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\begin{pmatrix}
tI_m&X\\
X^{\mathsf T}&tI_n
\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.
\]
Feasibility of the block inequality implies \(t\ge0\). Hence an affine expression constrained by a spectral-norm upper bound can be canonicalized using one positive-semidefinite constraint of order \(m+n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rectangular matrix has spectral norm at most a scalar exactly when a corresponding symmetric block matrix is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Norm Graphs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block-semidefinite spectral-norm epigraph formula is coherent and properly scoped to real rectangular matrices, but it lacks a cited source and specific locator.

children.title: Nuclear Norm Graphs
children.top_down_role: Graph representations for the sum of singular values.

assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\)
\(t\in\mathbb{R}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|X\|_*\le t\iff\exists W\in\mathbb{S}^m,Z\in\mathbb{S}^n:\begin{pmatrix}W&X\\X^{\mathsf T}&Z\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,\ (\operatorname{tr}W+\operatorname{tr}Z)/2\le t\).

notation.meaning: Real symmetric matrices of order k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted semidefinite representation of the nuclear-norm epigraph for rectangular real matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), the nuclear norm satisfies
\[
\|X\|_*
=\min_{W\in\mathbb{S}^m,\ Z\in\mathbb{S}^n}
\left\{\frac12\bigl(\operatorname{tr}W+\operatorname{tr}Z\bigr):
\begin{pmatrix}W&X\\X^{\mathsf T}&Z\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\right\}.
\]
Consequently, \(\|X\|_*\le t\) holds exactly when there exist \(W\in\mathbb{S}^m\) and \(Z\in\mathbb{S}^n\) satisfying the displayed block positive-semidefinite constraint and \((\operatorname{tr}W+\operatorname{tr}Z)/2\le t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nuclear-norm epigraph is the projection of a block positive-semidefinite constraint with a trace upper bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Nuclear Norm Graphs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lifted semidefinite representation of the nuclear-norm epigraph is coherent and fits the container, but no supporting citation or locator is supplied.

children.title: Ky Fan Norm Graphs

knowledge_statements.title: Ky Fan Norm Graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semidefinite epigraph representation using the symmetric dilation of a rectangular matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(1\le k\le\min\{m,n\}\), and \(D(X)=\begin{bmatrix}0&X\\X^{\mathsf T}&0\end{bmatrix}\). Then the epigraph of the Ky Fan \(k\)-norm has the representation \[t\ge \sum_{i=1}^{k}\sigma_i(X)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists s\in\mathbb{R},\ Y\in\mathbb{S}^{m+n}:\ Y\succeq0,\quad Y+sI_{m+n}\succeq D(X),\quad ks+\operatorname{tr}(Y)\le t.\] Thus an affine matrix expression may be canonicalized by substituting it for \(X\) in these linear matrix inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The epigraph of the sum of the largest k singular values is the projection of an explicit semidefinite system built from the symmetric dilation.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\)
\(1\le k\le\min\{m,n\}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge\|X\|_{(k)}\) is equivalent to the displayed semidefinite feasibility system.

notation.meaning: The i-th largest singular value of X.

children.title: Singular-Value Multiplicity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Graph geometry at repeated singular values and ordered-sum transition points.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Value Multiplicity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variational characterization of cutoff multiplicity in Ky Fan singular-value sums.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), let \(D(X)\) be its symmetric dilation and let \(1\le k\le\min\{m,n\}\). Then \[\sum_{i=1}^{k}\sigma_i(X)=\max\{\operatorname{tr}(P D(X)):0\preceq P\preceq I,\ \operatorname{tr}(P)=k\}.\] If \(\sigma_k(X)>\sigma_{k+1}(X)\), with \(\sigma_{k+1}(X)=0\) when \(k=\min\{m,n\}\), the maximizing positive-eigenspace projector is fixed by the leading singular subspaces. If \(\sigma_k(X)=\sigma_{k+1}(X)>0\), maximizers can redistribute rank within the tied eigenspace, so the supporting certificate is nonunique although the graph value is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tie at the singular-value cutoff makes the Ky Fan supporting projector nonunique, but it does not alter the norm value or graph representation.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\)
\(1\le k\le\min\{m,n\}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A positive cutoff tie yields multiple maximizing certificates for the same Ky Fan graph value.

notation.meaning: A positive semidefinite contraction of trace k.

children.title: Schur-Complement Graph Templates
children.top_down_role: Semidefinite graph families organized by Schur-complement transformations.

knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Graph Templates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic positive-semidefinite block template with strict and generalized boundary forms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{S}^{p}\), \(C\in\mathbb{S}^{q}\), and \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}\). If \(A\succ0\), then \[\begin{bmatrix}A&B\\B^{\mathsf T}&C\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad C-B^{\mathsf T}A^{-1}B\succeq0.\] If merely \(A\succeq0\), the block inequality is equivalent to \((I-AA^{\dagger})B=0\) and \(C-B^{\mathsf T}A^{\dagger}B\succeq0\). Consequently, matrix-fractional and quadratic graph inequalities become affine semidefinite constraints whenever their denominator block and range conditions satisfy the applicable form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block positive-semidefinite constraint represents a matrix-fractional inequality through the ordinary or generalized Schur complement.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{S}^{p},\ C\in\mathbb{S}^{q}\)
\(B\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed block inequality is equivalent to the corresponding Schur-complement conditions.

children.title: Matrix-Fractional Graphs
children.top_down_role: Positive-definite-domain graph forms for matrix fractional expressions.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Fractional Graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph of the matrix fractional map on its positive-definite denominator domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Y\in\mathbb{S}^{p}_{++}\), \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}\), and \(T\in\mathbb{S}^{q}\), the matrix fractional map is \(F(X,Y)=X^{\mathsf T}Y^{-1}X\). Its semidefinite epigraph is \[F(X,Y)\preceq T\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \begin{bmatrix}Y&X\\X^{\mathsf T}&T\end{bmatrix}\succeq0.\] Hence, when \(X\) and \(Y\) are affine expressions and \(Y\succ0\) is enforced by the domain, the graph inequality is canonicalized as one affine linear matrix inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The upper graph of X-transpose Y-inverse X is exactly a block positive-semidefinite constraint when Y is positive definite.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\in\mathbb{S}^{p}_{++}\)
\(X\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}\)
\(T\in\mathbb{S}^{q}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^{\mathsf T}Y^{-1}X\preceq T\) if and only if the displayed block matrix is positive semidefinite.

knowledge_statements.title: Log-Determinant Graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hypograph and extended-value epigraph representations for the matrix log-determinant atom.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb{S}^{n}_{++}\), define \(f(X)=\log\det X\), a concave spectral function. Its hypograph is \[\operatorname{hypo}f=\{(X,t)\in\mathbb{S}^{n}\times\mathbb{R}:X\succ0,\ t\le\log\det X\}.\] Equivalently, the convex atom \(g(X)=-\log\det X\) is extended by \(g(X)=+\infty\) for \(X\notin\mathbb{S}^{n}_{++}\), and its epigraph is \(\{(X,t):X\succ0,\ -\log\det X\le t\}\). Any canonical graph representation must retain the strict positive-definite domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The log-determinant hypograph, equivalently the negative-log-determinant epigraph, is represented only on the strict positive-definite domain.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb{S}^{n}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The log-determinant hypograph and negative-log-determinant epigraph are the displayed domain-restricted sets.

notation.meaning: The cone of real symmetric positive-definite matrices.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Entropy Graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph representation of negative von Neumann entropy with its closed positive-semidefinite extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\in\mathbb{S}^{n}_{+}\) with spectral decomposition \(X=U\operatorname{diag}(\lambda)U^{\mathsf T}\), define the negative matrix entropy by \[h(X)=\operatorname{tr}(X\log X)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\lambda_i\log\lambda_i,\qquad 0\log0:=0.\] Set \(h(X)=+\infty\) outside \(\mathbb{S}^{n}_{+}\). The function \(h\) is closed and convex, and its graph template is the epigraph \[\operatorname{epi}h=\{(X,t)\in\mathbb{S}^{n}\times\mathbb{R}:X\succeq0,\ \operatorname{tr}(X\log X)\le t\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The graph template for negative matrix entropy is the positive-semidefinite-domain epigraph of the convex spectral sum of lambda log lambda, continuously extended at zero.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb{S}^{n}_{+}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h(X)=\operatorname{tr}(X\log X)\) is closed and convex with the displayed epigraph.

notation.meaning: Continuous scalar entropy convention at zero.

children.title: Positive-Definite Domain Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Boundary behavior as matrices approach singularity or leave the positive-definite domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Definite Domain Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contrasting boundary behavior of log-determinant and entropy matrix atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_j\in\mathbb{S}^{n}_{++}\) converge to \(X\in\mathbb{S}^{n}_{+}\) with \(\det X=0\). Then \[-\log\det X_j\longrightarrow+\infty.\] Thus a singular matrix cannot be admitted to the closed extended-value domain of negative log determinant with finite value. In contrast, \(\operatorname{tr}(X_j\log X_j)\to\operatorname{tr}(X\log X)\) under the convention \(0\log0=0\). Therefore canonicalization must not replace the strict domain of a log-determinant atom by the closed semidefinite domain valid for matrix entropy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative log determinant diverges at singular matrices, whereas matrix entropy extends continuously there; their positive-definite boundary rules are not interchangeable.
assumptions_latex: \(X_j\succ0\) and \(X_j\to X\succeq0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(-\log\det X_j\to+\infty\), while \(\operatorname{tr}(X_j\log X_j)\to\operatorname{tr}(X\log X)\).

notation.meaning: Convergence in any matrix norm in finite dimension.

children.title: Affine-Composition Recognition

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Composition Recognition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Syntactic and dimensional criterion for recognizing an affine argument of a graph atom.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An expression \(a(x)\) is recognized as affine on a real finite-dimensional variable space when it can be normalized to \[a(x)=A x+b,\] where \(A\) is a fixed linear map and \(b\) is fixed, with output shape matching the selected atom. For an expression \(f(a(x))\), affine composition is admissible precisely when \(a(x)\) is affine, \(a(x)\in\operatorname{dom}f\) is enforced, and the graph template for \(f\) accepts that output type. Substitution of \(Ax+b\) into an affine conic graph preserves convexity and conic representability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composition is affine-recognized when its argument normalizes to a fixed linear map plus offset and satisfies the atom's type and domain requirements.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) lies in a finite-dimensional real vector space.
\(f\) has a declared graph template and domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Recognized affine substitution preserves the declared conic graph representation of \(f\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: affine precomposition preserves convexity and conic graph form

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine-recognition condition is plausible and internally coherent, but no inspectable citation supports the canonicalization and admissibility claims.

children.title: Monotone-Composition Recognition
children.top_down_role: Use of monotonicity and argument curvature metadata in graph selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone-Composition Recognition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar disciplined-convex composition rule driven by curvature and argument monotonicity metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^{r}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be convex. For each argument \(i\), suppose \(f\) is nondecreasing, nonincreasing, or unrestricted on the relevant domain. The composition \(x\mapsto f(g_1(x),\ldots,g_r(x))\) is recognized as convex when every \(g_i\) is respectively convex, concave, or affine, and the tuple lies in \(\operatorname{dom}f\). If \(f\) is concave, reversing convex and concave in these argument rules recognizes a concave composition. Unknown monotonicity requires the corresponding argument to be affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composition recognition combines outer curvature, argumentwise monotonicity, inner curvature, and domain metadata using the standard disciplined-convex rules.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) has declared curvature and argumentwise monotonicity.
\((g_1(x),\ldots,g_r(x))\in\operatorname{dom}f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated metadata combinations certify convexity or concavity of the composition.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated disciplined-convex composition principle is standard and correctly scoped, but it requires an authoritative source with a specific theorem or section locator.

children.title: Expression Admissibility Metadata System

children.title: Sign Recognition
children.top_down_role: Static recognition of expression sign information used for graph selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Sign Recognition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound propagation of sign metadata through an expression tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Associate each expression \(e\) with a certified value set \(S(e)\subseteq\mathbb{R}\). Declare \(e\) nonnegative when \(S(e)\subseteq[0,+\infty)\), nonpositive when \(S(e)\subseteq(-\infty,0]\), zero when \(S(e)=\{0\}\), and unknown otherwise. For an atom \(e=f(e_1,\ldots,e_r)\), compute any sound enclosure satisfying \[f(S(e_1),\ldots,S(e_r))\subseteq S(e).\] Sign metadata may authorize a graph rule only when the required inclusion is certified; failure to certify a sign must remain unknown rather than be treated as the opposite sign.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sign recognition is sound set propagation: a sign is asserted only when every possible expression value lies in the corresponding half-line.
assumptions_latex: Each leaf has a sound value-set enclosure.
Each atom provides a sound enclosure rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every reported sign contains all values attainable by the expression.

notation.meaning: A certified enclosure of all possible values of expression e.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sound-enclosure formulation is coherent, but the record supplies no inspectable source for this abstract-interpretation model of sign metadata.

children.title: Domain Recognition
children.top_down_role: Static recognition of expression domains and admissible graph implementations.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain Recognition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive admissibility condition for the effective domain of a composed expression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an expression \(e(x)=f(e_1(x),\ldots,e_r(x))\), its recognized domain is \[D(e)=\left\{x:x\in\bigcap_{i=1}^{r}D(e_i),\ (e_1(x),\ldots,e_r(x))\in\operatorname{dom}f\right\}.\] A graph template for \(e\) is admissible only if its generated constraints enforce every inherited child-domain condition and the outer-atom condition. When a domain is open, such as \(X\succ0\) for \(\log\det X\), replacing it by its closure is invalid unless the atom's chosen extended-value convention proves equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The domain of a composition is the intersection of child domains and the preimage of the outer atom's domain, including strict-boundary conventions.
assumptions_latex: Every atom has a declared effective domain.
Every child expression has recursively recognized domain metadata.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D(e)=\bigcap_iD(e_i)\cap(e_1,\ldots,e_r)^{-1}(\operatorname{dom}f)\).

notation.meaning: The recursively recognized domain of expression e.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recursive domain formula and warning about open domains are mathematically sound, but the canonicalization requirement lacks an authoritative citation and locator.

children.title: Symmetry Recognition
children.top_down_role: Recognition of symmetric, Hermitian, or structurally invariant expression forms.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry Recognition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural criterion for admitting expressions to symmetric-matrix graph templates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A square matrix expression \(E(x)\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetry-certified when its expression rules establish \[E(x)=E(x)^{\mathsf T}\quad\text{for every admissible }x.\] Certification is preserved by fixed symmetric constants, symmetric variables, transpose-paired sums \(F+F^{\mathsf T}\), congruences \(A^{\mathsf T}SA\) with symmetric-certified \(S\), and real linear combinations of symmetric-certified expressions. Equality of dimensions alone does not certify symmetry. A template over \(\mathbb{S}^{n}\), including a semidefinite or log-determinant graph, is selectable only after this identity is certified or explicitly imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix expression is symmetry-recognized only when structural rules prove equality with its transpose for every admissible variable value.
assumptions_latex: \(E(x)\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) for every admissible \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Symmetric-matrix graph templates are admissible only if \(E(x)=E(x)^{\mathsf T}\) is certified or constrained.

notation.meaning: The space of real symmetric n by n matrices.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The structural symmetry rules are sound and fit the recognition container, but no inspectable source supports the stated template-selection requirement.

children.title: Metadata Conflict Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where inferred sign, domain, or symmetry information is incomplete or incompatible.

assumptions_latex: Each expression node has independently inferred curvature, sign, domain, symmetry, and dimension metadata.
An admissibility rule specifies the metadata combinations accepted by the parent operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The node lies on a metadata conflict boundary precisely when its inferred metadata set is nonempty but has empty intersection with the combinations admitted by its parent rule.

notation.meaning: metadata assignments inferred for expression node v
metadata assignments admitted by the parent rule
