children.title: Quadratic-Objective Extraction
children.top_down_role: Recognition and extraction of supported quadratic objective structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Objective Extraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalization of a recognized convex quadratic objective for a QP backend.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the canonicalized objective be \(q(x)=\tfrac12 x^{\mathsf T}P x+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\), where \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(P=P^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(d\in\mathbb R\). Quadratic-objective extraction emits the QP data \((P,c)\) and records \(d\) as an objective offset. If an input quadratic is given by a nonsymmetric matrix \(Q\), replace it by \((Q+Q^{\mathsf T})/2\). The extracted backend objective plus the recorded offset equals \(q(x)\) for every \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recognize a convex quadratic, symmetrize its matrix, emit the Hessian and linear coefficient, and retain the constant as an objective offset.
assumptions_latex: The objective is a finite quadratic function on \(\mathbb R^n\).
The symmetric quadratic coefficient is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(x)=\tfrac12 x^{\mathsf T}P x+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\) with backend data \((P,c)\) and recoverable offset \(d\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits, but no evidence is supplied. The nonsymmetric-matrix instruction is ambiguous unless the original quadratic convention is stated, since the relation between Q and the backend Hessian P depends on whether the input uses x^TQx or one-half x^TQx.

children.title: Piecewise-Affine Term Lowering
children.top_down_role: Lowering of compatible piecewise-affine components without general cone expansion.

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise-Affine Term Lowering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph lowering of convex piecewise-affine terms into linear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}(a_i^{\mathsf T}x+b_i)\) be a convex piecewise-affine term used in a nondecreasing minimization context. Introduce \(t\in\mathbb R\), replace \(f(x)\) by \(t\), and add \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x+b_i\le t\) for every \(i\). For fixed \(x\), the least feasible \(t\) equals \(f(x)\); hence minimizing the lifted expression preserves the optimal value and the projection of optimal solutions onto the original variables. No nonpolyhedral cone is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace a maximum of affine functions by an epigraph variable constrained above every affine piece, yielding a purely linear QP-compatible formulation.
assumptions_latex: The piecewise-affine term is a finite maximum of finitely many affine functions.
Its surrounding minimization expression is nondecreasing in the term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)=\min\{t:\ a_i^{\mathsf T}x+b_i\le t\text{ for all }i\}\).

notation.meaning: epigraph variable for the piecewise-affine term

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The epigraph lowering is mathematically standard and the representation kind fits, but the record supplies neither a citation nor an explicit standard-field rationale as required for this candidate claim.

children.title: Affine-Constraint Extraction
children.top_down_role: Extraction and normalization of affine constraints for QP backends.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Constraint Extraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalization of affine equalities and inequalities into QP matrix data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and suppose every canonical constraint is affine. After moving constants and variable terms to fixed sides, stack equalities as \(A x=b\) and two-sided inequalities as \(\ell\le Gx\le u\), allowing components of \(\ell\) or \(u\) to be infinite when supported. A one-sided constraint is represented by setting the absent bound to the corresponding infinity. The extracted tuple \((A,b,G,\ell,u)\) defines exactly the same feasible set as the original affine constraint family, subject to the backend's fixed row ordering and sign convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize and stack affine equalities and inequalities into matrices and bound vectors that define exactly the original feasible set.
assumptions_latex: All constraints are affine in the backend variable vector \(x\).
The backend supports the selected equality and bound conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:\text{original constraints hold}\}=\{x:\ Ax=b,\ \ell\le Gx\le u\}\).

notation.meaning: stacked equality matrix and right-hand side

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine normalization is precise and the representation kind fits, but no citation or explicit standard-field rationale is supplied. Backend support for infinite bounds is correctly conditional but still requires evidence.

children.title: QP Eligibility Recognition
children.top_down_role: Structural conditions that permit direct symbolic QP lowering.

knowledge_statements.title: QP Eligibility Recognition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recognition criterion for routing a convex symbolic model directly to a quadratic-program backend.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A finite-dimensional model is QP-eligible when, after affine substitution and constant removal, it has the form
\[
\underset{x\in\mathbb R^n}{\operatorname{minimize}}\quad \tfrac12 x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x+r
\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\;Gx\le h,
\]
where \(P\in\mathbb S_+^n\), and all displayed coefficients are numerical data. Eligibility requires every auxiliary-variable defining relation to be affine and forbids any remaining nonlinear constraint, nonpolyhedral cone membership, integer restriction, or variable-dependent quadratic constraint. Under these conditions the model is a convex quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model is QP-eligible exactly when its objective is convex quadratic and all remaining constraints and auxiliary definitions are affine or componentwise linear inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) is continuous.
\(P\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model is admissible for a convex QP interface without conic lifting.

notation.meaning: positive-semidefinite symmetric matrices of order n

children.title: Structure-Preserving QP Routes
children.top_down_role: Canonicalization routes that retain quadratic problem structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Preserving QP Routes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonicalization route retaining quadratic objective structure and polyhedral constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a QP-eligible expression graph, introduce variables only for affine subexpressions, propagate affine maps until the objective is assembled as \(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x+r\), and collect affine equalities and inequalities as \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\). Symmetrize the quadratic coefficient by replacing \(P\) with \((P+P^{\mathsf T})/2\), verify \(P\succeq0\), and remove the constant \(r\) from the solver objective while retaining it for value recovery. Output \((P,q,A,b,G,h)\); reject this route if a nonaffine constraint or unsupported cone remains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonicalize eligible models by preserving the quadratic objective, collecting linear constraints, symmetrizing the Hessian, and emitting native QP data.
assumptions_latex: The input satisfies the QP eligibility condition.
All affine graph transformations preserve dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The emitted QP has the same feasible decisions and optimizer set as the input model, with objective values shifted only by the recorded constant \(r\).

children.title: Conic Fallback Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Model features that require departure from the QP target.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Fallback Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary at which native QP routing must yield to a conic representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A convex model lies beyond the native QP boundary if every exact graph representation available to the canonicalizer retains at least one constraint of the form \(F(x)\in K\), where \(K\) is nonpolyhedral, or retains a nonlinear convex constraint not reducible to affine equalities and componentwise affine inequalities. Standard triggers include \(\lVert Bx+d\rVert_2\le a^{\mathsf T}x+\beta\) and affine positive-semidefinite constraints. Such a model must use a compatible conic target unless an exact auxiliary-variable reformulation eliminates those primitives and restores QP eligibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonpolyhedral cone constraints or irreducible nonlinear convex constraints force conic fallback unless an exact reformulation restores quadratic-objective, linear-constraint form.
assumptions_latex: Only exact, continuous convex reformulations are admitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of QP eligibility after available exact rewrites requires conic routing.

notation.meaning: a closed convex cone used by the target interface

children.title: Cone-Free Backend Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of eligible canonical forms with nonconic solver interfaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Free Backend Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility predicate for solver interfaces accepting QP data but no explicit cone domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a backend accept continuous QP data \((P,q,A,b,G,h)\) with \(P\succeq0\), but no explicit cone membership. A canonical model is compatible with that backend precisely when it admits an exact formulation
\[
\underset{x}{\operatorname{minimize}}\quad \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x
\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\;Gx\le h,
\]
using only backend-supported bounds and affine rows. Merely encoding nonnegativity through inequalities is cone-free at the interface; second-order, semidefinite, exponential, or power-cone membership is incompatible unless eliminated by an exact supported reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone-free QP backend is compatible only when the canonical model uses a convex quadratic objective and supported affine rows or bounds.
assumptions_latex: The backend supports continuous convex QPs.
Compatibility concerns exact formulations, not approximations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compatibility holds if and only if no unsupported explicit or implicit nonpolyhedral cone primitive remains.

children.title: Canonical Orientation Convention System

children.title: Objective-Sense Normalization
children.top_down_role: Canonical treatment of minimization and maximization conventions.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Sense Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between maximization and the canonical minimization objective sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a feasible set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and an extended-real objective \(f:C\to\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\}\), objective-sense normalization replaces
\[
\underset{x\in C}{\operatorname{maximize}}\ f(x)
\quad\text{by}\quad
\underset{x\in C}{\operatorname{minimize}}\ -f(x).
\]
The feasible set and optimizer set are unchanged, while the optimal values satisfy \(p_{\min}=-p_{\max}\) whenever either value is interpreted consistently in the extended reals. A minimization objective is left unchanged. If convex canonicalization is required, the maximized \(f\) must be concave, equivalently \(-f\) must be convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convert maximization to minimization by negating the objective; feasible points and optimizers stay fixed, and the optimal value changes sign.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the common feasible set.
Extended-real signs are interpreted consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in C}f(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}(-f(x))\) and \(p_{\min}=-p_{\max}\).

notation.meaning: optimal values before and after normalization

children.title: Inequality-Orientation Normalization
children.top_down_role: Canonical orientation choices for inequality constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Inequality-Orientation Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conversion of scalar affine inequalities to one canonical orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For scalar functions \(g,h:X\to\mathbb R\), the inequality \(g(x)\ge h(x)\) is normalized to
\[
h(x)-g(x)\le0,
\]
whereas \(g(x)\le h(x)\) is normalized to \(g(x)-h(x)\le0\). Equivalently, an affine row \(a^{\mathsf T}x\ge b\) becomes \((-a)^{\mathsf T}x\le-b\). These transformations preserve the feasible set exactly. When a Lagrange multiplier is attached after normalization, its sign convention must correspond to the chosen residual orientation rather than the original printed relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Move all scalar inequalities to a common less-than-or-equal-to-zero form, negating both sides when necessary and preserving feasibility.
assumptions_latex: The inequalities are interpreted componentwise when vector-valued.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The normalized and original inequalities define identical feasible sets.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: algebraic equivalence of inequality orientations
authoritative locator for canonicalization convention pending
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar identities are correct and fit the container, but the assumptions introduce an unformalized componentwise vector extension while the statement declares scalar-valued functions. children.title: Equality-Orientation Conventions
children.top_down_role: Sign and ordering conventions used for equality constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Orientation Conventions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical residual convention for scalar or vector equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For maps \(g,h:X\to\mathbb R^m\), normalize the equality \(g(x)=h(x)\) as the zero residual
\[
g(x)-h(x)=0.
\]
The reversed residual \(h(x)-g(x)=0\) defines the same feasible set, so a deterministic canonicalizer may select either orientation by a fixed ordering rule. If an equality multiplier \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) is stored with the residual, reversing the residual requires replacing \(y\) by \(-y\) to leave the Lagrangian term \(y^{\mathsf T}(g(x)-h(x))\) invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent every equality by a zero residual; reversing that residual preserves feasibility but requires negating its stored multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) and \(h\) have the same codomain \(\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Residual reversal preserves the constraint set, and the paired transformation \((r,y)\mapsto(-r,-y)\) preserves the Lagrangian contribution.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: equality residual and multiplier sign invariance
authoritative locator for orientation convention pending

children.title: Orientation-Reversal Bookkeeping
children.top_down_role: Metadata needed to interpret results after orientation changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Orientation-Reversal Bookkeeping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign-map tracking for recovering residuals and dual variables after canonical orientation changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each scalar or vector constraint residual \(r_i(x)\), store a sign \(s_i\in\{-1,1\}\) and emit the canonical residual \(\widehat r_i(x)=s_i r_i(x)\). For an equality, or for an inequality whose cone order is reversed consistently, map the canonical multiplier \(\widehat y_i\) back by \(y_i=s_i\widehat y_i\). Then
\[
y_i^{\mathsf T}r_i(x)=\widehat y_i^{\mathsf T}\widehat r_i(x).
\]
Record the same sign in primal-residual and dual-solution metadata; output recovered residuals \(r_i=s_i\widehat r_i\) and multipliers \(y_i=s_i\widehat y_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Track one sign per reversed constraint and apply it to recovered residuals and multipliers so the Lagrangian pairing remains unchanged.
assumptions_latex: Each reversal is multiplication of the complete residual by \(-1\).
Inequality dual domains are transformed consistently with orientation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stored sign map permits exact recovery of original residual and multiplier conventions.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sign invariance of the residual-multiplier pairing

children.title: Cone-to-Cone Bridge Reductions
children.top_down_role: Equivalent transformations between cone interfaces with different primitive domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Cone-to-Cone Bridge Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact lifted transformations between selected standard cone interfaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A cone-to-cone bridge replaces \(F(x)\in K\) by affine equations and memberships in target cones whose projection onto \(x\) equals the original feasible set. Two exact primitive bridges are
\[
t\ge0\iff (t,0)\in\mathcal Q_2,
\qquad
(t,u)\in\mathcal Q_{m+1}\iff
\begin{pmatrix}t&u^{\mathsf T}\\u&tI_m\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,
\]
where \(\mathcal Q_{m+1}=\{(t,u):\lVert u\rVert_2\le t\}\). Applied blockwise, these identities embed nonnegative-orthant constraints into second-order cones and second-order-cone constraints into semidefinite cones without changing projected feasible decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bridge cone interfaces through exact affine liftings, such as embedding nonnegativity into a second-order cone and a second-order cone into a PSD constraint.
assumptions_latex: All bridge equations are imposed exactly.
Projection discards only introduced auxiliary coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted target-cone system projects exactly onto the source-cone feasible set.

children.title: Quadratic-to-Conic Bridges
children.top_down_role: Exact target-dependent conversion from quadratic structure to conic structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-to-Conic Bridges
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rotated-second-order-cone epigraph representation of a positive-semidefinite quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and choose \(R\) with \(P=R^{\mathsf T}R\). The quadratic epigraph has the exact representation
\[
t\ge\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px
\iff
(t,1,Rx)\in\mathcal Q_{m+2}^{r},
\]
where \(\mathcal Q_{m+2}^{r}=\{(a,b,u):2ab\ge\lVert u\rVert_2^2,\ a\ge0,\ b\ge0\}\). Consequently, minimizing \(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x\) over conic-representable constraints is equivalent to minimizing \(t+q^{\mathsf T}x\) with the displayed rotated-cone constraint and the same remaining constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor a PSD quadratic and represent its epigraph by one rotated second-order-cone constraint, yielding an exact linear-objective conic model.
assumptions_latex: \(P\succeq0\).
\(P=R^{\mathsf T}R\) with \(R\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted conic problem has the same feasible decisions, optimizer set, and objective values as the quadratic formulation.

children.title: Conic-to-Quadratic Recognition
children.top_down_role: Recognition of conic representations that admit a quadratic target.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(d\in\mathbb R\).
All variables and data are real.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The norm inequality is equivalent to the displayed quadratic inequality together with \(c^{\mathsf T}x+d\ge0\); the quadratic residual is convex exactly when \(A^{\mathsf T}A-cc^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: affine data defining the SOC constraint
Hessian coefficient of the squared quadratic residual

review_flags: distinguishes QP, convex QCQP, and nonconvex quadratic syntax
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recognition of second-order-cone constraints that admit a target-supported convex quadratic-and-affine description.

source_refs.locator: 3.1 Conic quadratic problems: Preliminaries p. 79

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(d\in\mathbb R\). The second-order-cone constraint
\[
\lVert Ax+b\rVert_2\le c^{\mathsf T}x+d
\]
is equivalent to
\[
(Ax+b)^{\mathsf T}(Ax+b)\le(c^{\mathsf T}x+d)^2,
\qquad c^{\mathsf T}x+d\ge0.
\]
The quadratic residual obtained by moving the squared right-hand side to the left is convex if and only if \(A^{\mathsf T}A-cc^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\). Hence this bridge yields a convex quadratically constrained formulation only under that matrix condition and only for a target supporting convex quadratic constraints. A backend supporting quadratic objectives but only affine constraints remains incompatible unless an exact simplification makes the constraint affine. Squaring without the nonnegativity side condition is not equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SOC constraint is equivalent to its squared quadratic inequality together with a nonnegative right-hand side. The resulting quadratic constraint is convex exactly when its Hessian coefficient is positive semidefinite, and it is usable only by a target supporting such constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Conic-to-Quadratic Recognition

source_witnesses.locator: 3.1 Conic quadratic problems: Preliminaries p. 79

children.title: Target-Dependent Representation Choice
children.top_down_role: Choice of quadratic or conic representation based on backend capabilities.

knowledge_statements.title: Target-Dependent Representation Choice
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection rule among exact quadratic and conic canonical representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal R(M,T)\) be the exact canonical representations of model \(M\) accepted by target \(T\). A target-dependent canonicalizer must choose some \(R^*\in\mathcal R(M,T)\); if this set is empty, the target is incompatible. Among accepted exact representations, a deterministic policy may minimize a declared cost tuple such as
\[
C_T(R)=(\text{unsupported primitives},\ \text{cone blocks},\ \text{auxiliary variables},\ \text{nonzeros}),
\]
ordered lexicographically. Thus a native QP representation may be preferred for a QP target, while an epigraphic second-order-cone representation may be preferred for a conic target, without changing mathematical equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose an exact representation accepted by the target, using a declared deterministic cost rule; different backends may legitimately receive different equivalent forms.
assumptions_latex: Candidate representations preserve projected feasible decisions and objective values.
Target capabilities are known before selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selection from \(\mathcal R(M,T)\) preserves model semantics; emptiness of \(\mathcal R(M,T)\) certifies target incompatibility.

notation.meaning: exact representations of model M accepted by target T

source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry
source_refs.locator: 3.3 Special Cases and Structure Exploitation p. 86

review_flags: cost tuple is a canonicalization policy rather than a universal theorem

children.title: Bridge Exactness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on equivalence, recoverability, or supported target conversion.

knowledge_statements.title: Bridge Exactness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness criterion for quadratic epigraphs represented by rotated second-order cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric. A real factor \(R\) satisfying \(Q=R^{\mathsf T}R\) exists exactly when \(Q\succeq0\). Under this condition, \(t\ge x^{\mathsf T}Qx\) is equivalent to \((t,\tfrac12,Rx)\in\mathcal Q_r\), where \(\mathcal Q_r=\{(u,v,w):u\ge0,\ v\ge0,\ 2uv\ge\lVert w\rVert_2^2\}\). If \(Q\not\succeq0\), the quadratic is nonconvex and no exact projection-preserving representation of this epigraph by convex conic constraints exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard rotated-cone bridge is exact precisely for positive-semidefinite quadratic forms; an indefinite quadratic epigraph cannot have an exact convex conic lift.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\).
The bridge must preserve the complete epigraph under projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\succeq0\iff\operatorname{epi}(x^{\mathsf T}Qx)=\{(x,t):(t,\tfrac12,Rx)\in\mathcal Q_r\}\) for some real \(R\).

notation.meaning: A factor satisfying Q = R-transpose R.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role and mathematics are appropriate, including the rotated-cone scaling and the obstruction from nonconvexity, but no cited source with a specific locator supports the exactness boundary or impossibility claim.

children.title: Slack-Equality Normalization Calculus
children.top_down_role: Canonical organization of equalities, inequalities, and introduced slack variables.

children.title: Slack-Variable Introduction
children.top_down_role: Canonical placement of introduced slack variables for inequality representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Slack-Variable Introduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalization of affine inequalities into cone-constrained equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a closed convex cone and let \(F(x)=Ax+b\). The conic inequality \(F(x)\in K\) is equivalent to introducing \(s\in\mathbb R^m\) and imposing \(Ax+b-s=0\) together with \(s\in K\). Projection of the lifted feasible set onto the \(x\)-coordinates recovers the original feasible set, and every feasible \(x\) has the unique compatible slack \(s=Ax+b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace an affine conic inequality by an equality to a new cone-constrained slack; projection preserves feasibility and the slack is uniquely determined.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax+b\in K\iff\exists s\in K:\ Ax+b-s=0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is precise and fits slack-variable introduction, but the record contains no citation or inspectable locator.

children.title: Equality Elimination
children.top_down_role: Removal of eligible equality constraints before solver-data assembly.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space elimination of consistent affine equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider variables \(z\in\mathbb R^n\) subject to \(Ez=d\), where the system is consistent. Choose one solution \(z_0\) and a matrix \(N\) whose columns form a basis of \(\ker E\). Then every equality-feasible point is represented uniquely as \(z=z_0+Ny\) when \(N\) has linearly independent columns. Substituting this expression into the objective and remaining constraints eliminates \(Ez=d\) without changing attainable objective values or the projected feasible solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A consistent affine equality can be removed by parameterizing its solution set with a particular solution and a null-space basis.
assumptions_latex: \(E\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\) and \(d\in\operatorname{range}(E)\).
The columns of \(N\) form a basis of \(\ker E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{z:Ez=d\}=\{z_0+Ny:y\in\mathbb R^{n-\operatorname{rank}E}\}\).

notation.meaning: A particular solution of the equality system.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The null-space representation is mathematically correct and fits equality elimination, but no source with a specific locator is cited.

children.title: Equality Retention
children.top_down_role: Preservation of equality blocks for solver-native handling.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality Retention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion for retaining affine equalities in canonical solver data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a canonical problem with constraints \(Ez=d\) and \(Gz+h\in K\), equality retention represents the feasible set directly as \(\{z:Ez=d,\ Gz+h\in K\}\). This representation is exact without rank assumptions on \(E\). It preserves the original coordinates and equality dual variables, while possibly retaining redundant rows; any row compression must therefore preserve the affine set \(\{z:Ez=d\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keeping affine equalities explicitly is always exact, preserves coordinates and equality multipliers, and tolerates redundant rows.
assumptions_latex: \(E,G\) and \(d,h\) have compatible finite dimensions.
\(K\) is a convex cone accepted by the canonical target.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_{\mathrm{ret}}=\{z:Ez=d,\ Gz+h\in K\}\) is the unchanged canonical feasible set.

notation.meaning: Feasible set under explicit equality retention.
Product cone for the conic constraints.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle appropriately describes exact retention of affine equalities, including redundant rows, but it lacks a cited source and locator.

children.title: Slack Recovery Maps
children.top_down_role: Result mappings associated with introduced slack coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Slack Recovery Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of introduced slacks from canonical primal coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the lifted constraint \(Ax+b-s=0\) with \(s\in K\), define the recovery map \(\rho(x)=Ax+b\). Every feasible canonical pair satisfies \(s=\rho(x)\), so \(\rho\) reconstructs the unique slack from the original coordinates. Conversely, if \(x\) satisfies \(Ax+b\in K\), then \((x,\rho(x))\) is lifted-feasible. Thus projection onto \(x\) and slack recovery are mutually inverse between the original feasible set and the lifted feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The affine residual uniquely recovers an introduced slack, giving a bijection between original feasible points and lifted feasible pairs.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\).
The slack equality is \(Ax+b-s=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\mapsto(x,\rho(x))\), with \(\rho(x)=Ax+b\), bijects \(\{x:Ax+b\in K\}\) and \(\{(x,s):Ax+b-s=0,\ s\in K\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine recovery map and bijection are precise and match the leaf, but the record supplies no supporting citation with a locator.
