children.title: Reduction-Chain Attribution
children.top_down_role: Association of dual information with the transformations that produced it.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduction-Chain Attribution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stagewise provenance representation for certificates transported through exact canonicalization reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_0\xrightarrow{R_1}P_1\xrightarrow{R_2}\cdots\xrightarrow{R_k}P_k\) be exact reductions, and let \(T_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_{i-1}\) transport valid certificates backward across stage \(i\). For a terminal certificate \(z_k\in\mathcal C_k\), define \(z_{i-1}=T_i(z_i)\). Its reduction-chain attribution is the trace \(\bigl((R_i,T_i,z_i,z_{i-1})\bigr)_{i=1}^k\), and its original-problem meaning is \(z_0=(T_1\circ\cdots\circ T_k)(z_k)\). Attribution is valid only when every stage records the variable, constraint, and cone-block correspondences needed to verify \(z_{i-1}\in\mathcal C_{i-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A terminal certificate is attributed by transporting it backward through every recorded reduction and retaining the stagewise objects and correspondences that justify its original-problem meaning.
assumptions_latex: Each \(R_i\) is an exact reformulation on the certificate class under consideration.
Each transport map \(T_i\) is defined on every valid certificate produced at stage \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_0=(T_1\circ\cdots\circ T_k)(z_k)\) is the certificate attributed to the original problem.

notation.meaning: Valid certificate set at stage i.

children.title: Expression-Rewrite Growth
children.top_down_role: Growth of canonical expression structure under recursive rewriting.

knowledge_statements.title: Expression-Rewrite Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case structural growth under recursive atom expansion, with and without subexpression memoization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every rewritten expression node produces at most \(b\) child nodes requiring further rewriting, and every rewrite chain has depth at most \(d\). Expanding one root as a tree creates at most \(1+b+\cdots+b^d=(b^{d+1}-1)/(b-1)\) nodes when \(b>1\), and at most \(d+1\) when \(b=1\). For \(r\) roots the bound is multiplied by \(r\). If structurally identical subexpressions are memoized, each of the \(U\) distinct rewrite states is expanded once, so the stored rewrite DAG has at most \(U\) expanded states and at most \(bU\) generated dependency edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recursive rewriting can grow exponentially with depth when represented as a tree, while memoization limits expansion to the number of distinct rewrite states.
assumptions_latex: The rewrite branching factor is bounded by \(b\ge 1\).
Every rewrite path has depth at most \(d\).
Memoization uses a sound structural-equivalence key when the DAG bound is invoked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Tree expansion is \(O(rb^d)\) for \(b>1\), whereas memoized expansion is \(O(U+bU)\) in stored states and edges.

notation.meaning: Number of distinct memoized rewrite states.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: bounded-branching tree and DAG counting
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits the growth leaf, and the bounded-tree and memoized-DAG counts are mathematically coherent. An inspectable source is still required to support their use as the canonicalization cost model.

children.title: Lift Size-Growth Metrics
children.top_down_role: Growth in auxiliary variables, constraints, and cone blocks.

children.title: Auxiliary-Variable Growth
children.top_down_role: Growth in lifted variable dimensions caused by graph reformulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-Variable Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive accounting of lifted scalar variables across distinct canonical atom instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal U\) be the set of distinct canonical atom instances after permitted sharing, and let \(a(u)\) be the number of new scalar variables introduced by the graph implementation of \(u\). If different instances receive disjoint auxiliary bundles, then the lifted problem contains \(n_{\mathrm{aux}}=\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}a(u)\) auxiliary scalar variables. Without sharing, occurrences form a multiset \(\mathcal O\) and the corresponding count is \(n_{\mathrm{aux}}^{\mathrm{occ}}=\sum_{o\in\mathcal O}a(o)\). Consequently, sound sharing never increases the count and saves \(n_{\mathrm{aux}}^{\mathrm{occ}}-n_{\mathrm{aux}}\) variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Auxiliary-variable growth equals the sum of local lift dimensions over distinct canonical atom instances; sound reuse removes duplicate contributions.
assumptions_latex: Each atom implementation declares a finite scalar lift dimension \(a(u)\).
Auxiliary bundles of nonshared instances are disjoint.
Shared instances have identical arguments and compatible graph semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(n_{\mathrm{aux}}=\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}a(u)\le\sum_{o\in\mathcal O}a(o)=n_{\mathrm{aux}}^{\mathrm{occ}}\).

notation.meaning: Scalar auxiliary dimension of instance u.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role fits auxiliary-variable growth, and the additive count follows under the stated disjointness and sharing conventions. No source with a specific locator supports those canonical graph-implementation conventions.

children.title: Constraint-Count Growth
children.top_down_role: Growth in canonical equality and inequality counts.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Count Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive row and scalar-cone constraint accounting for canonical graph implementations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the unreduced model contain \(m_0\) scalar constraint rows. For each distinct canonical atom instance \(u\in\mathcal U\), let \(e(u)\) be its added affine-equality rows and let \(q(u)\) be the scalar dimension of its added conic membership constraints. When graph implementations contribute disjoint new rows, canonicalization produces \(m_{\mathrm{eq}}=m_{0,\mathrm{eq}}+\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}e(u)\) equality rows and \(m_{\mathrm{cone}}=m_{0,\mathrm{cone}}+\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}q(u)\) scalar conic rows. Thus the total scalar-row count is \(m=m_0+\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}(e(u)+q(u))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonical constraint growth is the original row count plus the equality and scalar conic rows contributed by each distinct graph implementation.
assumptions_latex: Constraint size is measured in scalar rows.
Each canonical atom implementation declares \(e(u)\) and \(q(u)\).
Shared graph implementations are counted once.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m-m_0=\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}(e(u)+q(u))\).

notation.meaning: Added affine-equality rows for instance u.
Added scalar conic dimension for instance u.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role fits constraint-count growth and the formulas are consistent when cone size is measured in scalar rows. A source is needed for this metric convention and the canonical graph accounting interface.

children.title: Cone-Block Growth
children.top_down_role: Growth in the number and aggregate size of cone blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Block Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Type-sensitive accounting of product-cone blocks introduced by canonical graph implementations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal T\) index primitive cone-block types, let \(B_{0,\tau}\) be the number of original blocks of type \(\tau\), and let \(b_\tau(u)\) be the number of such blocks introduced by a distinct canonical atom instance \(u\in\mathcal U\). If shared implementations are counted once, then \(B_\tau=B_{0,\tau}+\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}b_\tau(u)\) for every \(\tau\in\mathcal T\). If each type \(\tau\) has scalar dimension \(d_\tau\), the resulting scalar conic dimension is \(Q=\sum_{\tau\in\mathcal T}d_\tau B_\tau\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cone-block growth is the componentwise sum of the blocks introduced by distinct canonical atoms, while scalar conic dimension additionally weights each block by its dimension.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal T\) indexes cone types whose block dimensions \(d_\tau\) are fixed by the type convention.
The canonical cone is represented as an ordered product of primitive blocks.
Every atom implementation declares its block-type multiset.
Shared graph implementations contribute their blocks once.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_\tau-B_{0,\tau}=\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}b_\tau(u)\) for every \(\tau\in\mathcal T\), and \(Q=\sum_{\tau\in\mathcal T}d_\tau B_\tau\).

notation.meaning: Number of type-tau blocks contributed by instance u.
Total number of type-tau cone blocks.
Scalar dimension assigned to a type-tau block.

children.title: Shared-Lift Reuse
children.top_down_role: Size effects from reusing common lifted subexpressions.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Lift Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reuse of one lifted graph for repeated structurally identical subexpressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a subexpression \(s\) occurs \(k\ge 1\) times with identical arguments, curvature context, and graph implementation. If its graph uses \(a(s)\) auxiliary variables and \(c(s)\) scalar constraint rows, one shared epigraph or hypograph lift may replace \(k\) separate copies. The shared construction uses \(a(s)\) variables and \(c(s)\) rows instead of \(ka(s)\) and \(kc(s)\), saving \((k-1)a(s)\) variables and \((k-1)c(s)\) rows. Reuse is invalid when occurrences differ in arguments, parameters, sign-dependent domain conditions, or required graph orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identical compatible subexpressions may share one graph lift, saving all but one copy of its auxiliary variables and constraints.
assumptions_latex: All \(k\) occurrences denote the same subexpression under the canonicalizer's equivalence relation.
Their graph orientation and domain conditions coincide.
All consumers may reference the same lifted output variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reusable lift saves \((k-1)a(s)\) auxiliary variables and \((k-1)c(s)\) scalar rows without changing the represented feasible set.

notation.meaning: Auxiliary-variable count of the subexpression lift.
Scalar-row count of the subexpression lift.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: common-subexpression elimination with exact graph reuse
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle role fits shared-lift reuse, and the savings formulas are correct under the stated exact-sharing assumptions. A system or canonicalization source is required for the equivalence relation and feasible-set preservation claim.

children.title: Canonicalization Resource-Cost Model
children.top_down_role: Symbolic compilation, data construction, and storage costs.

children.title: Rewrite-Time Cost
children.top_down_role: Time consumed by symbolic graph rewriting and target recognition.

knowledge_statements.title: Rewrite-Time Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work bound for memoized recursive canonicalization of an expression DAG.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be the expression-state DAG processed by a memoizing canonicalizer. If matching and validating node \(v\in V\) costs \(p(v)\), constructing its replacement costs \(r(v)\), and traversing each dependency edge costs constant time, then \(T_{\mathrm{rw}}=O\!\left(|E|+\sum_{v\in V}(p(v)+r(v))\right)\). If \(p(v)+r(v)\le C\) for every \(v\in V\), then \(T_{\mathrm{rw}}=O(|E|+C|V|)\). Without memoization, the analogous bound applies to the occurrence tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Memoized rewrite time is linear in traversed dependencies plus the matching and replacement cost of each distinct expression state.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is the processed expression-state DAG.
Each distinct rewrite state is expanded at most once.
Dependency traversal has constant cost per edge.
The costs \(p(v)\) and \(r(v)\) include all local rule work.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{rw}}=O\!\left(|E|+\sum_{v\in V}(p(v)+r(v))\right)\), and under the uniform local bound \(p(v)+r(v)\le C\), \(T_{\mathrm{rw}}=O(|E|+C|V|)\).

notation.meaning: Vertices and dependency edges of the processed expression DAG.
Rule-matching and validation cost at v.

children.title: Data-Assembly Time
children.top_down_role: Time consumed while constructing numerical solver data.

knowledge_statements.title: Data-Assembly Time
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse assembly cost after symbolic canonicalization has fixed matrix coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N_{\mathrm{mat}}\) be the number of sparse matrix values emitted and \(N_{\mathrm{vec}}\) the number of dense vector values emitted after symbolic canonicalization fixes all coordinates and dimensions. If each value is evaluated once and inserted into a preallocated or amortized constant-time buffer, then \(T_{\mathrm{asm}}=\Theta(N_{\mathrm{mat}}+N_{\mathrm{vec}})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With precomputed sparse coordinates and amortized constant-time insertion, numerical assembly time is linear in emitted matrix entries and vector data, which is also an output-size lower bound.
assumptions_latex: Sparse coordinates and output dimensions are already known.
Each of the \(N_{\mathrm{mat}}+N_{\mathrm{vec}}\) numerical values is evaluated and emitted once.
Insertion into assembly buffers has amortized constant cost.
Materializing each emitted value requires at least constant work.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{asm}}=\Theta(N_{\mathrm{mat}}+N_{\mathrm{vec}})\).

notation.meaning: Number of emitted sparse matrix values.
Number of emitted dense vector values.

children.title: Symbolic-Memory Cost
children.top_down_role: Memory occupied by expression graphs, reductions, and structural metadata.

knowledge_statements.title: Symbolic-Memory Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Memory bound for expression DAGs, rewrite metadata, and symbolic sparse structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a symbolic canonicalizer retain \(V\) expression or rewrite nodes, \(E\) dependency edges, \(M\) rule and provenance records, and \(Z\) symbolic sparse-coordinate records. If every retained record and edge endpoint occupies \(O(1)\) machine words, then its symbolic memory satisfies \(S_{\mathrm{sym}}=O(V+E+M+Z)\). If each counted object requires at least one machine word, then \(S_{\mathrm{sym}}=\Theta(V+E+M+Z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symbolic memory is linear in retained DAG nodes, edges, metadata, and sparse-coordinate records under bounded-size records; sharing replaces occurrence-tree storage by DAG storage.
assumptions_latex: \(V,E,M,Z\in\mathbb N_0\) count retained nodes, edges, metadata records, and coordinate records, respectively.
Each node, edge endpoint, metadata item, and coordinate record occupies \(O(1)\) machine words.
Referenced numerical payloads are excluded from symbolic memory.
All retained symbolic objects are counted once.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{\mathrm{sym}}=O(V+E+M+Z)\), and under a constant positive per-object storage requirement, \(S_{\mathrm{sym}}=\Theta(V+E+M+Z)\).

notation.meaning: Counts of retained symbolic DAG nodes and edges.
Number of rule and provenance records.

children.title: Numeric-Storage Cost
children.top_down_role: Storage required for matrices, vectors, cone metadata, and index maps.

knowledge_statements.title: Numeric-Storage Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Machine-word storage for sparse canonical matrices, vectors, and cone metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the canonical numerical data contain matrices \(A\in\mathbb R^{m_A\times n_A}\) and \(G\in\mathbb R^{m_G\times n_G}\), stored in compressed sparse column format, vectors with total length \(L_{\mathrm{vec}}\), and cone metadata of length \(L_K\). If every numerical value and integer index occupies \(O(1)\) machine words, then \(S_{\mathrm{num}}=O(\operatorname{nnz}(A)+\operatorname{nnz}(G)+n_A+n_G+L_{\mathrm{vec}}+L_K)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numeric storage is linear in sparse nonzeros, column-pointer counts, vector lengths, and cone metadata, assuming compressed sparse column matrices and fixed-size numerical words.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m_A\times n_A}\) and \(G\in\mathbb R^{m_G\times n_G}\) use compressed sparse column storage.
Each numerical value and integer index occupies \(O(1)\) machine words.
The stored numerical vectors have total length \(L_{\mathrm{vec}}\).
Symbolic expression and provenance objects are excluded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{\mathrm{num}}=O(\operatorname{nnz}(A)+\operatorname{nnz}(G)+n_A+n_G+L_{\mathrm{vec}}+L_K)\).

children.title: Sparsity-Fill-In Coupling
children.top_down_role: Interaction between graph choices, canonical sparsity, and solver factorization structure.

children.title: Canonical Matrix Sparsity
children.top_down_role: Sparsity patterns produced by a selected canonical graph representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Canonical Matrix Sparsity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support bound induced by local affine dependencies in canonical graph constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) be the assembled canonical constraint matrix. For each row \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), let \(D_i\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be the scalar variables on which that row's affine expression depends. If assembly introduces no coefficient outside \(D_i\), then \(\operatorname{supp}(G_{i,:})\subseteq D_i\), so \(\operatorname{nnz}(G_{i,:})\le |D_i|\) and \(\operatorname{nnz}(G)\le\sum_{i=1}^m|D_i|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each canonical matrix row can be nonzero only on variables used by its local affine expression, bounding total nonzeros by summed row dependency sizes.
assumptions_latex: \(G\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) is assembled before any elimination or factorization.
Every canonical constraint row \(i\) has an explicitly recorded dependency set \(D_i\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
No algebraic preprocessing introduces coefficients outside those dependency sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{nnz}(G)\le\sum_{i=1}^m|D_i|\).

notation.meaning: Number of structurally nonzero entries of G.

children.title: Lift-Induced Fill-In
children.top_down_role: Additional structural coupling introduced by auxiliary variables or constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Lift-Induced Fill-In
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural fill introduced when auxiliary variables enlarge a canonical conic system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be the aggregate sparsity graph of a canonical system, and let an exact lift introduce auxiliary vertices \(W\), producing \(G'=(V\cup W,E')\). For an elimination ordering \(\pi\), recursively connect every pair of later neighbors of each eliminated vertex. If \(F_\pi(G')\) denotes the resulting added-edge set, then lift-induced fill is \[F^{\mathrm{lift}}_\pi=F_\pi(G')\setminus F_{\pi|_V}(G).\] Thus an exact lift can preserve the projected feasible set while increasing factorization storage and arithmetic through new elimination cliques.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Auxiliary variables may preserve the represented problem yet create additional elimination edges, increasing factorization cost beyond that of the unlifted sparsity graph.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) and \(G'\) are finite undirected sparsity graphs.
\(\pi\) is a complete elimination ordering of \(V\cup W\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F^{\mathrm{lift}}_\pi=F_\pi(G')\setminus F_{\pi|_V}(G)\) measures fill attributable to the lift.

notation.meaning: Edges added by elimination of graph G in ordering pi.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elimination-graph definition of sparse factorization fill

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the leaf, but no citation supports this particular set-difference definition of lift-attributable fill. A source or clarification is needed about how the original graph is embedded in the lifted graph and whether changes among original-variable edges are included.

children.title: Factorization Fill-In Exposure
children.top_down_role: Potential factorization structure implied by canonical solver data.

knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Fill-In Exposure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symbolic Cholesky cost exposed by the canonical matrix sparsity pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be symmetric positive definite with sparsity graph \(G\), and let \(L\) be the Cholesky factor obtained under ordering \(\pi\). If \(d_k\) is the number of later neighbors of the vertex eliminated at step \(k\) in the filled graph, then \[\operatorname{nnz}(L)=\sum_{k=1}^{n}(d_k+1),\qquad \operatorname{flops}(L)=O\!\left(\sum_{k=1}^{n}(d_k+1)^2\right).\] Hence canonicalization exposes factorization cost through the elimination cliques, not merely through \(\operatorname{nnz}(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cholesky storage and arithmetic are controlled by filled elimination degrees; a sparse canonical matrix can therefore still yield an expensive factorization.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb S_{++}^{n}\).
Symbolic and numerical elimination use the same ordering \(\pi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{nnz}(L)=\sum_k(d_k+1)\) and the factorization work is \(O(\!\sum_k(d_k+1)^2)\).

notation.meaning: Number of later neighbors at elimination step k.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role and elimination-degree formulas are standard and internally consistent, but the record supplies no inspectable sparse-Cholesky source locator.

children.title: Ordering Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Dependence of sparsity consequences on variable, constraint, or cone ordering.

knowledge_statements.title: Ordering Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A four-vertex example showing that fill depends on elimination order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be the path with vertices \(\{1,2,3,4\}\) and edges \(\{\{1,2\},\{2,3\},\{3,4\}\}\). Eliminating in order \(\pi_1=(1,2,3,4)\) adds no edge. Eliminating in order \(\pi_2=(2,1,3,4)\) first makes the later neighbors \(1\) and \(3\) adjacent, adding \(\{1,3\}\). Therefore \[|F_{\pi_1}(G)|=0<1=|F_{\pi_2}(G)|,\] although both orderings factor the same sparse matrix pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two elimination orders for the same path graph produce different fill, so canonical factorization cost is ordering-sensitive.
assumptions_latex: Eliminating a vertex completes its later-neighbor set to a clique.

notation.meaning: Fill edges generated by ordering pi.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is correct and fits Ordering Sensitivity, but no citation with a specific locator supports the elimination-fill convention being used.

children.title: Alternative Exact-Graph Cost Models
children.top_down_role: Comparison of multiple exact graph implementations for the same atom or model.

knowledge_statements.title: Alternative Exact-Graph Cost Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison rule for exact graph implementations of one atom.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and suppose two lifted sets \(C_i\subseteq X\times\mathbb R\times Z_i\) satisfy \[\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,t):\exists z_i\in Z_i,\ (x,t,z_i)\in C_i\},\qquad i\in\{1,2\}.\] The implementations are extensionally equivalent but need not be computationally equivalent. They must be compared by a cost vector such as \[c_i=(\dim Z_i,\ m_i,\ s_i,\ \phi_i),\] recording auxiliary dimension, constraint count, cone-block sizes, and predicted factorization fill. Exactness alone does not determine a preferred graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two lifts may represent exactly the same epigraph while differing in auxiliary size, cone structure, and predicted factorization fill.
assumptions_latex: Both projections equal the same epigraph exactly.
Costs are evaluated under a fixed canonical backend and ordering policy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_{X\times\mathbb R}C_1=\operatorname{proj}_{X\times\mathbb R}C_2\) does not imply \(c_1=c_2\).

notation.meaning: The ith exact lifted graph implementation.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact extended formulations can have unequal structural costs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle matches the comparison-oriented container and correctly distinguishes extensional exactness from structural cost, but the proposed cost model lacks an inspectable canonicalization or extended-formulation source.

children.title: Convex but Unrecognized Expressions
children.top_down_role: Convex expressions lacking a supported disciplined or canonical form.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex but Unrecognized Expressions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incompleteness of grammar-based convexity recognition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal G\) be an expression grammar with a sound compositional curvature checker \(R\). Soundness means \[R(e)=\mathrm{convex}\ \Longrightarrow\ f_e\text{ is convex on }\operatorname{dom}f_e.\] Recognition need not be complete: there may exist an expression \(e\) whose denotation \(f_e\) is convex but for which \(R(e)=\mathrm{unknown}\) because no permitted composition rule establishes its curvature. In that case rejection is a limitation of the recognition system, not a certificate that \(f_e\) is nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sound expression checker may reject a genuinely convex expression when its grammar or composition rules cannot certify convexity.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) uses only rules registered for the grammar \(\mathcal G\).
Each accepted curvature rule is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_e\text{ convex}\not\Rightarrow R(e)=\mathrm{convex}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sound rule systems need not be complete

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure boundary correctly distinguishes soundness from completeness and matches the node, but no disciplined-convex-programming source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Insufficient Expression Metadata
children.top_down_role: Recognition failures caused by unresolved sign, domain, curvature, or symmetry information.

knowledge_statements.title: Insufficient Expression Metadata
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metadata sufficiency condition for applying a registered composition rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an atom \(h(u_1,\ldots,u_k)\), a compositional curvature rule is applicable only if the metadata environment \(M\) proves every rule premise: the curvature of each \(u_i\), its required sign or interval, domain membership, and any required affine or matrix-symmetry property. Formally, for a registered premise set \(P_h\), recognition succeeds only when \[M\vdash P_h(u_1,\ldots,u_k).\] If a true premise is neither declared nor inferable, then \(M\nvdash P_h\), and the expression remains unrecognized even when its denotation has the claimed curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonical recognition fails when required sign, domain, curvature, affine, or symmetry facts are true but unavailable to the inference system.
assumptions_latex: The recognizer applies registered rules only after proving all their premises.
Missing metadata is not silently assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\nvdash P_h\) blocks the rule for \(h\), regardless of whether its premises are semantically true.

notation.meaning: Available expression metadata and inference facts.
Premises of the registered rule for atom h.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits metadata-driven recognition, but its all-premises-must-be-proved behavior is recognizer-dependent and requires a source describing the relevant rule system.

children.title: Unsupported Atom Graphs
children.top_down_role: Accepted mathematical atoms without an available exact graph implementation.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsupported Atom Graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recognition succeeds, but exact graph reduction is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an atom \(f\) be accepted with curvature and domain metadata, and let the canonical target language permit sets generated from a cone family \(\mathcal K\). Exact graph reduction requires a registered set \(C_f\) satisfying \[\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,t):\exists z,\ (x,t,z)\in C_f\},\] with \(C_f\) expressible using affine constraints and cones in \(\mathcal K\). If no such registered implementation is available, canonicalization must report an unsupported-graph failure; recognition of convexity alone does not authorize an approximate or inequivalent replacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An accepted convex atom cannot be canonically reduced when the target library lacks a registered exact epigraph graph for it.
assumptions_latex: The atom \(f\) is semantically accepted.
Canonicalization is required to preserve the epigraph exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{accepted}(f)\land\neg\exists C_f\text{ registered}\Rightarrow\text{unsupported-graph failure}.\)

notation.meaning: Cone family supported by the canonical target language.
A registered exact lifted epigraph representation of f.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact canonicalization requires an implemented graph reduction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure boundary accurately separates semantic atom recognition from availability of an exact registered graph implementation, but it has no inspectable implementation or canonicalization source.

children.title: Unsupported Cone or Target Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Canonical structures incompatible with available solver interfaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsupported Cone or Target Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An exact canonical graph exists but cannot be transmitted to the selected backend.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose canonicalization produces \[Ax+b\in K_1\times\cdots\times K_m,\] where every \(K_j\) has a declared dimension and data representation. Let \(\mathcal I_S\) be the cone types, dimensions, and encodings accepted by solver interface \(S\). The model is directly dispatchable only if every block descriptor belongs to \(\mathcal I_S\). If some \(K_j\notin\mathcal I_S\) and no registered exact bridge rewrites it into supported blocks, dispatch must fail even though the canonical graph is mathematically valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid canonical conic model cannot be dispatched when its cone type, dimension, or encoding is unsupported and no exact bridge exists.
assumptions_latex: The canonical conic representation is exact.
Only registered exact interface bridges may alter cone blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists j\;(K_j\notin\mathcal I_S)\land\neg\text{exact bridge}\Rightarrow\text{interface failure}.\)

notation.meaning: Cone-block descriptors accepted by solver interface S.
The jth cone block in the canonical model.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: solver dispatch requires compatible cone encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure phenomenon fits the node, but no solver-interface source is cited. The text tests block descriptors against the interface while the formulas test the cone sets K_j themselves; a sourced version should distinguish a cone from its type, dimension, and encoding descriptor.

children.title: Lost or Misrepresented Domain Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Graph rewrites that mishandle domain closure or limiting behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Lost or Misrepresented Domain Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential-cone boundary omitted by a strict-perspective rewrite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the closed exponential cone by \[K_{\exp}=\operatorname{cl}\{(x,y,z):x>0,\ z\ge x\exp(y/x)\}.\] Its boundary includes \(\{(0,y,z):y\le0,\ z\ge0\}\). A rewrite that retains only the strict formula \(x>0\) has projection missing these boundary points; replacing \(x>0\) by \(x\ge0\) without separately specifying the limiting branch leaves \(y/x\) undefined at \(x=0\). Thus neither rewrite represents \(K_{\exp}\) exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The strict exponential perspective omits a genuine boundary branch, while naive substitution at zero is undefined; an exact graph must encode the closure explicitly.
assumptions_latex: The intended object is the closed exponential cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{(x,y,z):x>0,\ z\ge x\exp(y/x)\}\ne K_{\exp}\).

notation.meaning: Closed exponential cone under the displayed coordinate convention.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: closure convention for the exponential cone

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exponential-cone boundary counterexample is mathematically consistent under the displayed coordinate convention and fits the leaf, but the closure formula and limiting boundary branch need an authoritative cone-definition locator.

children.title: Nonclosed Projected Graphs
children.top_down_role: Projection regimes where closure affects representability or attainment.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonclosed Projected Graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A closed convex lifted set whose coordinate projection is not closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[C=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x>0,\ y\ge 1/x\}.\] The set \(C\) is convex and closed in \(\mathbb R^2\): approaching \(x=0\) while remaining in \(C\) forces \(y\) to diverge. Nevertheless, its projection onto the first coordinate is \[\operatorname{proj}_x C=(0,\infty),\] which is not closed. Hence projection of a closed convex lifted graph need not preserve closedness, and replacing the projection by its closure can add unattained boundary points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex lift can project to a nonclosed set; automatically closing that projection changes exact representability and may add unattained points.
assumptions_latex: Projection is the coordinate map \((x,y)\mapsto x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\text{ is closed and convex}\), but \(\operatorname{proj}_x C=(0,\infty)\) is not closed.

notation.meaning: Closed convex epigraph of the reciprocal function on the positive half-line.

children.title: Auxiliary Recession Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Lifted directions that obscure boundedness, attainment, or solution interpretation.

children.title: Auxiliary-Variable Unboundedness
children.top_down_role: Unbounded lifted coordinates that need not imply unbounded model variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-Variable Unboundedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbounded lifted fibers can coexist with bounded projected feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq X\times Z\) be a nonempty closed convex lift and \(P=\operatorname{proj}_X C\). For \(x\in P\), define the fiber \(C_x=\{z:(x,z)\in C\}\). Auxiliary-variable unboundedness occurs when some \(C_x\) is unbounded even though \(P\) is bounded. For example, \[C=\{(x,z)\in\mathbb R^2:x=0,\ z\ge0\}\] has \(P=\{0\}\) but \(C_0=[0,\infty)\). Thus boundedness of the original variables does not imply boundedness of an exact lifted feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted formulation may have unbounded auxiliary fibers even when its projected feasible set is a bounded singleton.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is interpreted as a lifted feasible set.
Only the \(X\)-coordinate is part of the original model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\text{ bounded}\not\Rightarrow C\text{ bounded}.\)

notation.meaning: Auxiliary fiber above original point x.
Projection of the lifted set onto original variables.

children.title: Lifted Recession Directions
children.top_down_role: Recession behavior introduced or exposed within lifted representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Recession Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recession directions of a lift that disappear under projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq X\times Z\) be a nonempty closed convex set and let \(P_X:X\times Z\to X\) be the coordinate projection. Its recession cone is \[\operatorname{rec}C=\{d:(u+\lambda d)\in C\text{ for every }u\in C\text{ and }\lambda\ge0\}.\] A purely lifted recession direction is a nonzero \(d=(d_x,d_z)\in\operatorname{rec}C\) satisfying \(P_Xd=d_x=0\). Such a direction generates an unbounded auxiliary ray above every feasible original point without producing a recession direction in the projected variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A purely lifted recession direction is a nonzero recession direction whose original-variable component vanishes, creating auxiliary rays invisible in projection.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(X\) and \(Z\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\in(\operatorname{rec}C\cap\ker P_X)\setminus\{0\}\) is a purely lifted recession direction.

children.title: Spurious Nonattainment Signals
children.top_down_role: Apparent attainment failures caused by auxiliary geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(P=\{x:\exists y,(x,y)\in Q\}\), and the objective is \(f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An unbounded auxiliary sequence alone does not establish nonattainment of the original problem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes auxiliary divergence from genuine failure of primal attainment.

source_refs.locator: 3.3.4 The geometry of the feasible sets expressed with different variables p. 51

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \((x^\star,y^\star)\in Q\) minimizes \(f(x)\) over \(Q\), and suppose a nonzero \(d\in\mathbb{R}^m\) satisfies \((0,d)\in\operatorname{rec}Q\). Then \((x^\star,y^\star+td)\in Q\) and \(f(x^\star)=f(x^\star)\) for every \(t\geq0\). Hence the lifted problem is attained even though it possesses minimizing sequences whose auxiliary components diverge. A diagnostic that infers nonattainment solely from \(\|y_k\|\to\infty\) therefore produces a spurious nonattainment signal whenever the projected components remain at an attained optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted optimizer may generate an unbounded auxiliary ray while its projected decision remains optimal and attained; auxiliary divergence alone is not evidence of nonattainment.
knowledge_statements.title: Spurious Nonattainment Signals

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3.4 The geometry of the feasible sets expressed with different variables p. 51

children.title: Recovery Ambiguity Under Recession
children.top_down_role: Limits on interpreting recovered solutions in the presence of lifted recession.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m\) is a closed convex lift of \(P\).
The original decision is recovered by the projection \(\pi_x(x,y)=x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Recovery is well-defined only modulo auxiliary fibers and auxiliary recession directions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery ambiguity caused by nonunique or recession-unbounded auxiliary fibers.

source_refs.locator: 3.3.4 The geometry of the feasible sets expressed with different variables p. 51

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in P\), define \(F(x)=\{y:(x,y)\in Q\}\). If \(F(x^\star)\) contains distinct points, or if some nonzero \(d\) satisfies \((0,d)\in\operatorname{rec}Q\), then the lifted representatives of \(x^\star\) are nonunique and may be unbounded. Nevertheless, every \((x^\star,y)\) with \(y\in F(x^\star)\) has the same primal recovery \(\pi_x(x^\star,y)=x^\star\). Any recovery rule depending on a particular auxiliary representative is ambiguous unless it is constant on each fiber and invariant under such recession displacements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Auxiliary representatives can be nonunique or unbounded under recession. Primal recovery remains valid only when the inverse map is constant on every auxiliary fiber.
knowledge_statements.title: Recovery Ambiguity Under Recession

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3.4 The geometry of the feasible sets expressed with different variables p. 51

children.title: Lift Quality-Size Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Exact or relaxing representations with avoidable size or weak numerical geometry.

children.title: Weak Lift Geometry
children.top_down_role: Lifted representations with poor geometric strength or conditioning.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Lift Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weakness refers to facial degeneracy of a nonempty, otherwise exact finite-dimensional conic lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\{Ax+By-b:(x,y)\in Q\}\), and let \(F_{\min}\) be the minimal face of \(K\) containing \(S\). The exact lift \(Q\) has weak lift geometry when \(F_{\min}\subsetneq K\). Equivalently, no \((x,y)\in Q\) satisfies \(Ax+By-b\in\operatorname{int}K\). Thus exactness of the projection \(P=\{x:\exists y,(x,y)\in Q\}\) does not imply strict feasibility in the chosen ambient cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty exact conic lift has weak lift geometry when all feasible slacks lie in a proper face of the ambient cone, equivalently when the lifted formulation has no strictly feasible point.
assumptions_latex: \(n,m,q\) are positive integers, \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^q\) is a closed convex cone with nonempty interior, \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times n}\), \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times m}\), and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^q\).
\(Q=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m:Ax+By-b\in K\}\) is nonempty and projects exactly onto \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact projection does not prevent a nonempty lift from lacking strict feasibility or having all its slacks in a proper face of \(K\).

notation.meaning: minimal face of the ambient cone containing all feasible lifted slacks

children.title: Redundant Lift Components
children.top_down_role: Avoidable auxiliary variables, constraints, or cone blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Lift Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic redundancy means removable within a specified admissible class of conic representations, not merely duplicated syntax.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The auxiliary block \(z\) is redundant relative to \(\mathcal C\) when there exists a formulation \(Q'=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m:G'(x,y)\in K'\}\in\mathcal C\) that contains no \(z\)-block and satisfies \[\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exists y\in\mathbb{R}^m,\exists z\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell},\ (x,y,z)\in Q\}=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exists y\in\mathbb{R}^m,\ (x,y)\in Q'\}=P.\] If the objective is \(f:P\to\mathbb{R}\) and depends only on \(x\), this replacement preserves all feasible objective values and hence the optimal value. Redundancy does not require \(z\) to be uniquely determined by \((x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An auxiliary block is redundant within an admissible representation class when an exact formulation in that class can omit the block without changing the projected feasible set; objectives depending only on the original variables are then preserved.
assumptions_latex: \(n,m,\ell,q\) are positive integers, \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^q\) is a closed convex cone, and \(G:\mathbb{R}^{n+m+\ell}\to\mathbb{R}^q\) is affine.
\(Q=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m\times\mathbb{R}^{\ell}:G(x,y,z)\in K\}\) is a conic lift of \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(\mathcal C\) is the specified admissible class of conic representations in which elimination is being assessed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The block \(z\) is redundant relative to \(\mathcal C\) exactly when an admissible formulation without it preserves the projected feasible set.

children.title: Oversized Exact Representations
children.top_down_role: Exact graph representations whose size exceeds available alternatives.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) has two exact conic lifts \(Q_1\) and \(Q_2\).
Lift size is measured by auxiliary dimension and total cone-block dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactness alone does not imply that a lift is size-efficient.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates projection exactness from economy of an extended conic formulation.

source_refs.locator: 6.4 Constructing Semidefinite Representations p. 271
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\pi_x(Q_1)=\pi_x(Q_2)=P\), so both lifts are exact. If \(s(Q_1)>s(Q_2)\), then \(Q_1\) is oversized relative to \(Q_2\) despite representing exactly the same set. More generally, a family \(Q_k\) is oversized when \(\pi_x(Q_k)=P\) for every \(k\) while \(s(Q_k)\to\infty\). Repeating a valid cone block or adjoining redundant variables produces such a family, showing that exactness places no upper bound on representation size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact lifts of the same set can have arbitrarily different sizes; redundant variables or repeated cone blocks can enlarge a representation without changing its projection.
knowledge_statements.title: Oversized Exact Representations

source_witnesses.locator: 6.4 Constructing Semidefinite Representations p. 271
